Chapter 3: The Search for Quality—Beyond Subject and Object
As the journey rolls on, the father just can’t let go of one word: Quality. It sounds simple, right? But the more he tries to pin it down, the more it slips through his fingers.
Is Quality something you can measure, like horsepower or temperature? Or is it something you just feel—something totally personal?
He keeps circling back to these questions, and honestly, they just won’t leave him alone.
But here’s the thing—this isn’t just some abstract puzzle for him.
Every time he tweaks the motorcycle, picks a spot to camp, or listens to his son, he’s making choices about what’s good, what feels right, what matters.
Most of us do this without really thinking about it.
We know when a meal tastes amazing, or when a conversation just clicks.
But if someone asks us to explain why, it gets fuzzy, doesn’t it?
The father remembers his younger self—the guy who became obsessed with finding a real, solid definition for Quality.
Driven by a need to understand, he dove headfirst into philosophy.
He read the classics, wrestled with ideas from the ancient Greeks all the way to modern thinkers.
At first, he hoped there’d be a tidy framework that would make sense of it all.
But the deeper he went, the more he realized that this question—what is Quality, really?—is at the heart of every big idea.
And it stubbornly refuses to fit in any neat box.
The problem, he saw, is that most philosophies split the world in two: there’s the subject—the person thinking—and the object—the thing being thought about.
But Quality? It doesn’t fit on just one side.
It’s not just a property of things, and it’s not just a feeling in your head.
It shows up in the space between—in the relationship, in the spark of engagement, in the living moment of experience.
That realization changed everything for him.
Instead of chasing answers in abstract theories, he started paying attention to the reality of daily life.
He noticed that the best moments—fixing a stubborn engine, sharing a simple meal, having a heart-to-heart—were all marked by a kind of harmony.
It’s that feeling when things just fit together, when everything clicks.
That, he realized, is Quality in motion.
But this search isn’t without its shadows.
His younger self got so wrapped up in the quest for answers that he lost touch with the world around him.
The drive for clarity turned isolating, even a little dangerous.
He remembers this breakdown—how it haunts him as they travel.
It’s a reminder that digging too deep, questioning everything, can sometimes carry a heavy cost.
Still, just going with the flow, never asking why, isn’t the answer either.
Living without reflection means missing out on all the richness that comes from really being engaged.
The challenge, he realizes, is to walk that middle path—to seek understanding while staying grounded in the real, immediate experience of life.
As the miles slip by, the father opens up about these thoughts with his son—sometimes through quiet conversations, sometimes through stories.
Chris listens.
Sometimes he looks puzzled, other times he’s clearly intrigued.
He senses, even if he doesn’t have the answers, that these questions really do matter.
Their talks become a way of exploring together, searching for meaning right in the middle of the ordinary.
So, Quality becomes the thread running through their journey.
It’s not some fixed destination, but a direction—a way of living that values attention, care, and real presence.
It’s about finding meaning not in big theories, but in the details of daily life.
Whether it’s tightening a bolt, riding in rhythm with the road, or sharing a quiet moment, the father and son discover that Quality isn’t something you define.
It’s something you live.
